symptom.title: Repeated reauthorization
symptom.summary: An agent requests permission again for an action that remains covered by a clear, applicable authorization.

observation.p: After explicit, applicable authorization of an action, the agent asks the user to authorize materially the same action at least once more. No changed target, scope, consequence, unmet consent condition, or governing requirement makes renewed approval necessary.

how-to-recognize-it.p: Pair each permission question in the transcript with the earlier approval and the proposed tool action. Compare account, resource, recipient, operation, conditions, and timestamps to see whether the approval covers the later action.

Check tool permission events, session expiry, and governing instructions for a new gate. Use message provenance to distinguish a conversational question generated by the agent from an enforced platform prompt, and inspect whether an answer led to execution or another question.

lookalike.p: The operation now affects a different account, recipient, resource, or materially broader scope. It is not the same authorized action required by redundant permission.
A governing instruction or tool gate requires fresh approval at this stage or after expiry. This is the renewed-approval requirement excluded by redundant permission.
Earlier consent depended on an unmet or unverified condition. That consent is not yet applicable to the action, unlike the authorization in redundant permission.

what-to-record.p: Record the episode identifier and date, task type, model/client and harness versions, original approval text, scope, conditions, and each later permission request. Preserve proposed actions, prompt origin, applicable gate policies, changed circumstances, and expiry or context boundaries. Include authorized actions attempted, redundant requests, user reply counts, approval-to-execution delay, unattended waiting time, and whether the task eventually ran or was abandoned.

example.p: Synthetic incident: the user approves clicking Continue on a named screen, but the agent asks twice more before clicking. The transcript, unchanged screen, and permission log show no new gate. Two extra replies are required and the click is delayed twelve minutes while the user is away.

Reported incident: Codex issue #48998 describes a conversational request to click Continue after that same action had already been approved. The reporter identifies the repeat by comparing the approval with the later question and says authorized unattended work stopped for another reply. The issue does not include the full transcript or a complete policy audit; total blocked time is not quantified.

Synthetic comparison: the user approves sending a draft to one colleague, then a proposed action targets a mailing list. Comparing recipient lists exposes the changed scope. One new approval concerns a different action rather than repeating permission for the original send.
